question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $a\geq 0,$ then 

$$
\sqrt{a^2} = a.
$$

First, notice that $9$ and $64$ are both perfect squares, where

$$
9=3^2,
$$

and

$$
64 = 8^2.
$$

So, to work out $\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{64}},$ we express $\dfrac{9}{64}$ as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{9}{64}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{{3}^{2}}{{8}^{2}}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{3\cdot 3}{8\cdot 8}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{3}{8}\cdot \frac{3}{8}} & = \\ \sqrt{{(\frac{3}{8})}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{3}{8} & \end{aligned}
$$
